working_title: The Tied Arm That Proved Your Blood Circulates
title: The Used-Up Blood (cold open, no chapter card)
set_language: Warm candlelit 17th-century world: dark oak, cream linen, brass, leather books, London fog. Body cutaways are clean, glowing illustrations (warm red arteries, cool blue veins), never anatomical gore. Say 'same 1616 London lecture room' or 'same Harvey study' for continuity; never 'same DNA'.
explorer_lock: NONE this part (STUDIO_PLAYBOOK §3: never in the first minute). Hands only, no faces before plate 07.
forbidden: HARD REJECT: Orbit robot; photoreal; Ken Burns or still push; gore, wounds, blood on skin, cut flesh or real animal organs (animal hearts only as Harvey's ink drawings); live or dead animals on a table; lava drip / molten bead; underside lamp bulb or shade cup; unfinished flat cards; garbled writing; unfinished Explorer hair; DNA helix; readable text or logos baked into the plate (labels and the De Motu Cordis title are added in the edit); twin Explorer; faces in the first two seconds of the film. Never say 'same DNA' or 'lab DNA' in a Veo prompt.
always_fails: garbled card text or wrong sums (2 oz, 1/8, 1000 checked by hand)
unfinished Explorer hair or melted face
gore: wound, blood on skin, cut flesh, real animal organs
a face in the first two seconds of the film
motion_lock: Real Veo camera and object motion on every plate. No freeze-pad, no loop, no Ken Burns.
quality_note: Flow Veo 3.1 on the Mac Mini CDP worker, benoats@googlemail.com only. Quality for anything with light (candles, glowing loop, stove heart) and every hero plate; Fast only for low-risk garnish. One plate at a time until the first KEEP; after 2 same-framing FAILs change the framing.
labels: White Didot italic side label, 1-4 words, one at a time, on the plate's first beat; added in the edit.

plates.vo_land: Your heart pumps more blood in half an hour than your whole body holds.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Frame 0: extreme close-up of a relaxed human wrist resting palm-up on dark oak, two fingertips pressed on the pulse, already moving. The skin is softly translucent cartoon skin: a warm glowing red stream races up the forearm in time with each beat; the camera follows it up the arm to a softly glowing beating cartoon heart. Hand and arm only, no face. No wound, no blood on skin. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: For fourteen hundred years, doctors taught that blood was made fresh from food and used up.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. An old oak table with a round loaf of bread and a pewter cup. They melt into a milky white glowing stream that flows into a smooth stylised glowing cartoon liver, which pours out bright warm red streams that spread into a faint outline of arms and legs and soak away like water into sand. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: So how did a band tied round an arm prove them wrong?
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. A bare upper arm resting on a candlelit oak table, arm and hand only, no face. Two hands wrap a strip of cream linen round the upper arm and pull it tight; below the band the veins on the forearm slowly swell into soft blue cords. Clean skin, no wound, no blood. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: By the end of this film, you'll know how one London doctor proved that your blood circulates, with a sum, a band, and tiny doors hidden inside your veins.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Dark oak desk by candlelight. A cream paper page with three short lines of large, clear brown-ink handwriting: '2 oz', '1/8', '1000'. A quill rests beside it and the candle flame flickers softly; camera glides slowly across the page. The numbers stay sharp and correct. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: (+3.6 s into) By the end of this film, you'll know how one London doctor proved that your blood circulates, with a sum, a band, and tiny doors hidden inside your veins.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same candlelit oak desk. A coiled strip of cream linen lies beside the page of sums; it slowly uncoils as if gently tugged from out of frame. Soft candle glow. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: (+7.0 s into) By the end of this film, you'll know how one London doctor proved that your blood circulates, with a sum, a band, and tiny doors hidden inside your veins.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Close-up of the back of a relaxed hand on the same oak desk, no face. A fingertip of the other hand presses a faint blue vein and slides along it; a tiny soft glow inside the vein stops at a small bump (a valve). Clean skin, no blood. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Every university taught the old idea.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. A university lecture hall around 1600: a thick leather book chained to a carved oak lectern; rows of students in dark robes copy from it by candlelight, quills moving. The camera glides slowly past the candles towards the book. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: If it was wrong, medicine had the human body backwards.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same lecture hall. A large painted anatomy chart of a stylised human figure, with the liver painted big and glowing gold at its centre, hangs on a cord; a draught makes the chart swing and slowly turn upside down. Candles gutter. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. London, 1616, at dusk. A narrow foggy lane of timber-framed houses; a carved stone doorway lit by candle lanterns (the Royal College of Physicians). The camera pushes slowly through the fog towards the door. No readable signs. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: (+2.7 s into) A short, dark-eyed doctor called William Harvey starts teaching anatomy at the Royal College of Physicians.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Inside a panelled, candlelit lecture room: William Harvey, a short man of about forty, olive skin, black hair to the collar, small pointed black beard and moustache, dark keen eyes, black physician's gown with a plain white falling collar, stands beside a large painted chart of the heart on an easel, lifts a long wooden pointer to it and turns to his audience with a keen look. Readable, finished face. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: He will spend the next twelve years on one question.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Close on Harvey's hand in a black sleeve dipping a quill and writing one large question mark on a blank cream page; the wet ink glints in candlelight; the camera eases in. Only the question mark on the page. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: And to answer it, he did something doctors almost never did.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same lecture room. The painted heart on Harvey's chart pulses, and its beat dissolves into the face of a brass table clock, ticking; Harvey's fingers tap the oak table once for each tick, counting. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.
